steps.name: PROGENy signalling pathway activity per sample
caveats: An activity score is an inference from a prior model, not a measurement; a high score is a hypothesis for follow-up
PROGENy weights were learned largely from perturbation experiments in cell lines; the footprint transfers to bronchial epithelium as an assumption, not a fact

With 12000 genes in the matrix, some pathways may match well under 500 responsive genes — a pathway with poor coverage has an unstable score and must be flagged rather than ranked alongside well-covered ones
Only 6 samples per group: a pathway score difference of modest size will have wide confidence intervals
steps.context: The question explicitly asks for footprint rather than membership: a PROGENy score is a weighted read-out of downstream perturbation-response genes, so a pathway can score high with no change in the expression of its own components, and the reverse. Human data, so the human PROGENy weights must be used, never the mouse ones.

steps.description: This step answers the research question. Load the human PROGENy footprint model of perturbation-responsive genes with per-gene weights for the 14 signalling pathways from the reference store (it is present as an R serialized data frame with gene, weight, p.value and pathway columns; rename to source/target/weight for decoupleR). Keep the top 500 responsive genes per pathway. Run decoupleR run_mlm on the per-sample log2-CPM matrix from T1S1 to obtain one activity score per pathway per sample (14 x 12). steps.name: Transcription factor activity on CollecTRI regulons

With 12000 genes profiled rather than a full transcriptome, regulon coverage is truncated for every TF — report the coverage distribution

steps.context: The TF layer is the regulator-level complement to the pathway footprint: both are inferences from prior knowledge networks over the same log-CPM matrix, so their agreement is a meaningful internal consistency check and their disagreement is informative. plan.title: Cytokine vs vehicle bronchial epithelium pathway footprint activity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The question asks which signalling pathways are active in the cytokine-stimulated bronchial epithelial samples relative to vehicle, judged by transcriptional footprint rather than by expression of pathway members. That is exactly the footprint-inference setting: PROGENy perturbation-response weights for the 14 signalling pathways, scored per sample with the decoupleR multivariate linear model, plus CollecTRI transcription-factor regulons scored with the univariate linear model as the regulator-level complement. No pathway-membership over-representation is planned, since it answers a different question.

The input is a 12000 x 13 gene-level count CSV from Salmon (one ID column plus 12 samples) with a 12 x 2 metadata table carrying condition, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. The record does not state whether the Salmon length correction was applied, so the first step must record that ambiguity and, because the counts may be fractional, round for the DESeq2/edgeR path and state the choice.

The profile flags sample_01 at roughly a quarter of the median library size. The procedure is explicit here: keep it, inspect it on PCA and the sample-distance heatmap, report its library size and detected-gene count beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. T1S1 does that and hands down an explicit keep/drop decision. Because the activity steps run on a per-sample log-CPM matrix rather than on a count model, a depth-driven sample cannot be down-weighted by a size factor there — so T1S1 also produces the CPM normalisation that neutralises depth, and T2S2/T2S3 must re-check whether sample_01 still sits apart in the score space and report a sensitivity analysis with it excluded.

T2S2 is the answer to the research question: PROGENy human weights (present in the reference store), top 500 responsive genes per pathway, mlm on the per-sample log matrix, then limma on the 14 x 12 score matrix for the treated-vs-control contrast with BH adjustment. T2S3 adds TF activity on CollecTRI (also present), ulm, minimum regulon size 5, signed edges kept, limma on scores with BH across regulators — a cytokine footprint should show as NFKB/JAK-STAT pathway activity with the corresponding STAT/IRF/RELA regulators, and agreement between the two layers is the internal check. T1S4 assembles the report with the reproducibility record and the standing caution that an activity score is an inference from a prior network, not a measurement. No ARACNe/VIPER network inference is planned: 6 per group is far below what mutual-information network inference needs, and SPIA (topology-aware impact) is not installed, so neither layer uses pathway graph topology and the report must say so.

steps.method: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap
PROGENy footprint model with decoupleR mlm

constraints: reproducibility_record = sessionInfo, seed, package versions, collection version, annotation release
activity_report_fields = network name, network version, input statistic, contrast, estimator, minimum regulon size, number of regulators tested, inference caution
Do not upgrade any activity score to a claim about a mechanism being engaged; a high score is a hypothesis for follow-up
caveats: Do not report only the concordant regulators and pathways; a selective concordance narrative is the main way this analysis becomes misleading

grounding.reason: No rule covers the report step as such; it carries the reproducibility record of R-0086@becf and the activity report fields and caution of R-0119@5f4d.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.
